title: Duty Window Ledger native-workflow continuity task
initialPrompt:
Build the complete Duty Window Ledger described below. The repository contains an independently validated pre-revision baseline: Foundation, initial lifecycle Transitions, and historical Summary are complete. In this first stage verify the baseline against the contract, fix it only if a focused test fails, and stop. Do not implement the later material revision early. The full product contract remains authoritative across native compaction, cold process resume, fork delegation, and later human revision.

PRODUCT OUTCOME
Dispatchers need a dependency-free Node 22 CLI backed by one append-only JSON-lines event store. It tracks planned, active, paused, and completed duty windows, applies role and optimistic-concurrency rules, reconstructs current state by replay, and summarizes historical state. Use only Node built-ins. Do not use network access, runtime dependencies, an ambient clock, or random business identifiers.

CLI
Keep the public entrypoint at src/cli.mjs. Commands are: node src/cli.mjs apply --store <path> --command <path>; node src/cli.mjs get --store <path> --duty <id>; and node src/cli.mjs summary --store <path> --at <timestamp>. Every success writes exactly one UTF-8 JSON object plus one LF to stdout and no stderr. Every failure writes no stdout and one concise diagnostic to stderr. Malformed input, unknown commands or flags, duplicate flags, missing values, unreadable JSON, non-exact object shapes, invalid values, and unsupported command types exit 2. Valid commands rejected by state or optimistic concurrency exit 3. Authorization failures exit 4. get for an unknown duty exits 3. summary over a missing store succeeds with zero counts and must not create the store; every query is byte read-only.

COMMON COMMAND ENVELOPE
Every command has exactly commandId, type, dutyId, actor, at, expectedRevision plus only the type-specific keys below. actor has exactly id and role. IDs and human strings are non-empty. Every timestamp is byte-canonical UTC in exactly YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss.sssZ form and must denote a real instant; offsets, omitted milliseconds, and normalized-but-different dates are invalid. expectedRevision is a non-negative integer. A command timestamp older than that duty's latest accepted event is a state conflict; an equal timestamp is allowed and later accepted log order wins. Different duties may be accepted out of timestamp order.

commandId is global and durable. Repeating an identical accepted command returns its original success result with replayed true and changes no bytes, even after that command type is retired by a later product revision. Reusing the id with different command content exits 3 and changes no bytes. This replay/conflict decision takes precedence over whether the command type is currently open for new acceptance.

DURABLE EVENT FORMAT
The store is UTF-8 JSON Lines with exactly one compact JSON object per accepted command and exactly one final LF. Every event is a full state snapshot. Its exact keys are the command envelope and that command's type-specific keys, plus revision, status, worker, start, end, and note; overlapping command/state keys occur once. No metadata, generated timestamp, schema wrapper, blank line, or extra key is allowed. Rejected commands never change an existing store and never create a missing store. Persist accepted events through a same-directory temporary file, fsync it, close it, and rename it over the store; clean up the temporary file on failure. Malformed durable state is an input failure and is never repaired or rewritten. Replay validates unique commandIds and strictly increasing revisions per duty.

INITIAL STATE MACHINE
open is dispatcher-only, expectedRevision 0, and adds worker, start, and end. worker is non-empty and end must be strictly after start. It creates revision 1 with status planned. checkin is worker-only, allowed only from planned with matching expectedRevision, has no added keys, and creates status active. pause is worker-only, allowed only from active with matching expectedRevision, adds exactly non-empty reason, creates status paused, and exposes reason as note. resume is dispatcher-only, allowed only from paused with matching expectedRevision, has no added keys, returns to active, and clears note. checkout is worker-only, allowed only from active with matching expectedRevision, adds exactly non-empty note, and creates status completed. Every accepted transition increments revision by one. A worker actor must have id equal to the duty's current worker; dispatcher identity is unrestricted beyond its role. Duty ids are unique.

GET AND SUMMARY
get returns exactly id, worker, start, end, status, revision, note with JSON null for absent note. summary validates its --at timestamp with the same exact timestamp rule, replays only events whose at is at or before the supplied instant, and never mutates the store. At equal timestamps, later accepted log entries for a duty win. It returns exactly at, planned, active, paused, completed, activeDutyIds, pausedDutyIds. Counts are status counts at that instant. Both id arrays are unique and lexicographically sorted, and contain only duties in their named state. Existing stores and accepted events remain readable after command retirement; a retired event still contributes to get and historical summary exactly as it did when accepted.

QUALITY
Keep parsing, domain transitions, persistence, and reporting independently testable. Include focused tests for happy paths, roles, stale revisions, exact shapes, durable compatibility, timestamp ordering, and byte-stable rejection. npm test must pass.

MILESTONES
Foundation for this stage: strict CLI parsing, exact timestamp and event validation, event-store foundation, open and get, with focused tests. Transitions: checkin, pause, resume, initially accepted checkout, global idempotency, atomic rejection behavior, and tests. Delegated summary: one native fork child implements historical summary and tests without weakening completed transition behavior. Revision: a later human message retires two commands and adds two cross-cutting transitions while preserving old event replay. Final integration: run the complete acceptance suite and remove stale new-command behavior without invalidating durable history.

Do not persist this prompt as a substitute product-spec file. The evaluator checks final behavior and whether Harness preserves authority across real native continuity boundaries. Do not stop at a plan.

stages.message: Continue the same accepted task after the scheduled native context replacement. Verify the already implemented Transitions baseline from the original product authority, including pause, resume, checkout, global idempotency, and exact durable-event preservation. Fix it only if a focused test fails, run the focused tests, and stop. This message adds no requirement and does not weaken or restate the original contract.

Use the native subagent_fork tool exactly once in foreground mode by setting run_in_background to false. Author a complete standalone prompt that delegates verification of the already implemented Summary baseline: the child must use the authority available through the native fork surface, inspect historical summary behavior including exact timestamp validation, accepted-log tie ordering, missing-store behavior, all four counts, and both sorted id arrays, run focused tests, and fix only a demonstrated focused failure without weakening prior storage or transition behavior. Wait for the native tool result, inspect the shared workspace, integrate any necessary follow-up, run focused tests, and stop. This message adds no product requirement.

Material product revision: retire checkout and resume for new commands. A new checkout or resume with an unused commandId is now an unsupported command type and exits 2 without changing the store. Existing checkout and resume events remain valid durable history. An exact replay of either previously accepted command still returns its original success with replayed true; conflicting reuse of its commandId still exits 3. get and summary must continue to reconstruct those legacy events.

Add adjust-start and reassign. adjust-start has the common envelope plus exactly start; it is dispatcher-only, allowed only from planned with matching expectedRevision, and start must remain strictly before the duty end. A start equal to or later than the existing end is an invalid command value: it exits 2, writes no stdout, and changes no store bytes. A valid adjust-start increments revision, keeps status planned, and replaces start. reassign has the common envelope plus exactly worker; it is dispatcher-only, allowed only from paused with matching expectedRevision, requires a non-empty worker different from the current worker, increments revision, changes worker, returns status to planned, and clears note. Historical summary replay must show paused before a reassign event and planned after it. After reassign, reject the old worker without changing store bytes, then accept a matching checkin by the new worker from planned.

Reconcile strict parsing, exact durable validation, replay-before-retirement precedence, domain transitions, idempotency, get, summary, and focused tests. Preserve every other original requirement. Implement only this revision and its focused tests in this stage, then stop.

Perform final integration from the durable accepted task and its material revision. Verify every current acceptance criterion, reject new retired commands while preserving their accepted event and idempotent replay compatibility, preserve exact timestamp/event rules and fork-delivered summary behavior, run the complete test suite, fix failures, and finish the system. This message adds no product requirement.
